newsitem.title: USA: Ill. House GOP opposes tax swap for schools - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ill. House GOP opposes tax swap for schools - paper.

text.p: More than three-quarters of the Illinois House Republican caucus opposes Gov. Jim Edgar's tax swap plan for public school funding, the Chicago Tribune reported Thursday.

Rep. Tom Johnson, R-West Chicago, told the Tribune that at least 45 of 58 House Republicans oppose Edgar's proposal for a 25 percent income tax increase to generate new revenue for schools and cut property taxes as much as $1.2 billion.
Edgar and legislative leaders have begun what the republican governor's aides call the final stages of talks for school funding changes.

The caucus straw poll could illustrate deep differences between Edgar and Republican House Leader Lee Daniels, who said that their is deep resistance to tax increases at a time of economic growth in the state, the newspaper said.

Republican Senate President James "Pate" Philip has floated a lesser income tax increase and Democratic House Speaker Michael Madigan has said he would be open to negotiating a school funding package that could include new performance requirements.

More school funding talks are scheduled for Thursday in Springfield. Legislators have set adjournment for May 23, but could meet until the end of May before the state constitution requirements for a super-majority vote take effect.
